featuresIntro.title: Everything that happens to an issue stays in the project.
featuresIntro.lead: Aether connects your team's daily work with planning and administration. Start with issues and boards, then configure the details around the way you work.

features.name: Boards
features.title: Adapt the board to your team’s process.
features.text: Arrange columns around workflow states. Filter issues and split them into swimlanes so each review can focus on the relevant team, epic or scope of work.

features.name: Backlogs and sprints
features.title: Plan a sprint with a goal and scope.
features.text: Choose issues from the backlog, set a goal and estimate the work. When the sprint ends, move unfinished issues back to the backlog or into another planned iteration.

features.name: Workflows
features.title: Define when an issue can change state.
features.text: A task may need review, more information or approval. Define states and transitions, with required fields that specify what must be ready before the next step.

features.name: Issues and collaboration
features.title: Descriptions, conversations and files with each issue.
features.text: Bring descriptions, priorities and assignees together with comments and files. Epics, subtasks and links show how an individual issue relates to the wider project.

features.name: Time tracking
features.title: Time records linked to specific tasks.
features.text: Start a timer or enter time worked against an issue. Collect entries into a period and submit it for approval. Later corrections preserve the change history.

features.name: Permissions
features.title: Define who sees a project and what they can change.
features.text: Invite your team and define project access. Roles, groups and permission schemes separate viewing a project, working on issues and project administration.

features.name: Search
features.title: Find issues and save the filters you need.
features.text: Search issue content and project fields. Saved filters and the LQL query language help you return to your own work, the team's issues or a particular release.
points: A view of work assigned to you

features.name: Releases and components
features.title: Assign issues to releases and components.
features.text: Link issues to a version to see what is ready and what still needs work. Components organise tasks by product area.

features.name: Reports
features.title: Review project progress and sprint delivery.
features.text: Check issue flow, completion times and sprint progress. Look at ageing tasks and current blockers to understand where to focus attention.

features.name: Moving your data
features.title: Bring your issues over from Jira.
features.text: Bring issues over from Jira using an export file, or load data in Aether’s format. Match the fields and check a trial result before moving data into the project.

features.name: API and extensions
features.title: Connect Aether to your team’s tools.
features.text: Use the REST API and extensions to exchange data and connect tools. Administrators define integration access and approve the permissions requested by installed packages.

features.name: History and audit
features.title: Review changes and actions.
features.text: Issue history shows how work progressed, while the audit trail records system actions. Use that context to explain a change and understand what happened in a project.

faq.title: Before you choose Aether
items: Who is Aether Lemric for?

For teams that manage projects through issues, work with boards or sprints, and want to connect planning with work history and time records. The Server edition supports installation in your own environment.
Can I install Aether on our servers?
Yes. Aether Server is designed for self-hosted installation. Your organisation manages the infrastructure, database, attachments, updates and backups.
Do we have to work in sprints?
No. You can use Kanban boards and the backlog without an active sprint. Sprints are available when your team plans work in iterations.
Can projects have different workflows and access rules?
Yes. Configure the process and access for a project. Permission schemes determine who can view it and perform individual actions.
How can we bring issues over from Jira?

Aether supports Jira export imports with mapping and dry runs. Check data coverage before changing tools; importing issues does not automatically migrate add-ons and every part of your Jira configuration.
How do we find out about licensing and deployment?
Email support@lemric.com. Tell us your team size, how you work and where you plan to install Aether so we can discuss release availability, licensing and deployment scope.

why.title: Why Aether Lemric
why.lead: A project management tool shapes the team's daily work. Aether brings issues, planning and time records together with installation in your own environment.
reasons: You want to see the whole path of a task
A task list is a starting point. Boards show the flow of work, workflows define the next step, and comments and history preserve decisions. See the current state and the path that led there.
Your team has its own working rules
Some projects need more than moving a card to done. Custom states, transitions and required fields accommodate review, approval and completion requirements.
You want to choose where data lives
Aether Server runs on infrastructure managed by your organisation. You set the policies for access, storage, updates and backups.
Owning a task, accessing a project and editing an issue are different responsibilities. Roles, groups and permission schemes help keep them distinct.
You want to connect the plan with actual work
Sprints and releases describe the plan. States, reports and time entries show delivery. In Aether, this information relates to the same issues.
You already have data and tools
Import dry runs help you evaluate moving issues. The REST API and extensions support connections to the other parts of your working environment.

about.title: Aether is built by Lemric.
about.lead: Aether Lemric is a new product, built on our experience in developing software, libraries and user interfaces.
about.title2: A tool for everyday project work
paragraphs: Sprint plans, task discussions and time records relate to the same work. In Aether, we connect them to issues so a project review can return to both the plan and what happened during delivery.
For some teams, where information is stored matters too. The Server edition supports installation in an environment managed by your own organisation.
principles: Different views of the same issues
Lists, boards and issue details use the same project data. Each view supports a different part of the team’s work.
Set states, transitions and permissions in configuration. Each project can have its own delivery and access rules.
We use our own Lemric libraries and Lemric DesignSystem. Shared interface components are used in Aether and other Lemric products.
